items.title: Claude Opus 5
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, their most powerful model yet. For your daily building, this means a massive jump in reasoning and coding capabilities, especially for handling complex state management and database relations in Next.js and Supabase. Try this week: Switch your Claude Code or Codex model to Opus 5 today and ask it to refactor the most complex API route in your AI-ingest project.

items.title: "We removed over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt for Opus 5 and Fable 5"
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic engineers optimized Claude Code for Opus 5 and Fable 5 by removing over 80% of its system prompt. This drastically reduces the baseline token cost of every single turn in your terminal sessions, making your development cycles much cheaper. Try this week: Run `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest` to update your CLI and immediately start saving tokens on your AI-ingest commits.

items.title: Claude Code hooks that block find/sed/cat, redirect to native tools
items.why_it_matters: A new open-source utility blocks Claude Code from wasting tokens on expensive shell commands like `find`, `sed`, and `cat`, forcing it to use cheaper native APIs instead. This is a direct fix for the token-drain that happens when Claude explores your Next.js directory. Try this week: Clone the `claude-no-bash-detour` repo and add the hooks to your local shell configuration to instantly lower your development costs.

items.title: AgentCost – local CLI,attributes token cost in Claude Code/Cursor/Codex sessions
items.why_it_matters: AgentCost is a new local CLI tool that tracks and attributes real-time token costs specifically for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex sessions. It gives you a clear breakdown of how much each feature you build actually costs you. Try this week: Run `pip install agentcost-cli` and keep it open in a split terminal during your next AI-ingest coding session to monitor your spend.

items.title: Show HN: Drive your real logged-in Chrome from Claude Code and Codex (MCP)
items.why_it_matters: This new Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets Claude Code and Codex control your actual logged-in Chrome browser. Instead of guessing if your UI works, Claude can now interact with your local development server directly. Try this week: Install the `browser-bridge` MCP server and ask Claude Code to open `localhost:3000` and test your AI-ingest signup flow.

items.title: Show HN: How well do you use Claude Code?
items.why_it_matters: Promptster released a free, open-source local tool designed to analyze your local Claude Code history and give you personalized coaching on how to save tokens. It helps you identify where your prompts are too wordy or where Claude is looping. Try this week: Clone the Promptster local analyzer from GitHub and run it against your Claude Code logs to see where you are leaking budget.

items.title: Show HN: Uploads.sh – the missing upload command for coding agents (open-source)
items.why_it_matters: Uploads.sh is a dead-simple, open-source terminal command for uploading files and logs to share with coding agents. It solves the annoying problem of trying to paste massive Next.js build errors or Supabase logs into your prompts. Try this week: Run `curl -F 'file=@package.json' https://uploads.sh` to quickly generate a clean link you can feed directly to Claude Code.
